gap: No result ChatGPT got states the capacity a kit's cycle count is measured down to: BLUETTI's 6,000 cycles for the Apex 300 end at 80%, Jackery's 6,000 for the HomePower 3600 Plus pack end at 70%, and Anker's 10,000 for the S5000 end at 60% (Anker's own blog gives the same battery 6,000 at 80%).
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), the Anker SOLIX kit collection (cited), PowerSized, Prepared States, Lights On Labs and our two Dealectric pages; solargenadvisor.com would not open (certificate error). StormWatts, PowerSized, Lights On Labs and the Anker collection page give no cycle life at all. Prepared States gives two cycle counts ('6,000+ cycles (maker)' for the Elite 300, '2,500 cycles' for the S2000 Pro) with no retention figure. Our under-$3,000 page has '6,000+ cycles to 80%' for the Elite 200 V2 only and 'over 3,500 charging cycles' for the R3500 with no end point. No page puts the three makers' end points side by side or says the S5000's 10,000 is a 60% figure. Surge is only partly new: Prepared States already lists several continuous/peak pairs, but none quotes Anker's 'peak power lasts only a fraction of a second'.
decides: It confirms rather than decides. At the same 80% line the Anker S5000 and BLUETTI Apex 300 are level at 6,000 cycles, so the S5000's '10,000 cycles' is no reason to pay more for it. The S5000 kit still has the lowest price per rated kWh cycled to 80% (about $0.12 against about $0.19 for the Apex 300 + 2× 500 W), because its battery is 1.8 times the size. ALLPOWERS gives the R3500 the lowest count (over 3,500) with no end point, so its low kit price buys fewer stated cycles. Separately, a shipping point could change the pick: Anker's S5000 page read today says orders placed on or after November 6 ship within 11 to 12 weeks, which conflicts with 'ships now' in the kits table. If that holds, the ships-now kits under $4,000 are the ALLPOWERS R3500 kits and the BLUETTI 5kWh RV kit.
